notes: v2.5.16 - required update. Inventory: consuming and splitting material was being refused as an overdraw when it was nothing of the kind - emptying a lot completely failed on lots whose quantity carries more decimals than the record holds, and 17 of 375 lots on hand were in that state. It got worse with use, because a partial consume leaves exactly the remainder that blocks the next attempt. Issuing material to a project splits the lot first, so the whole consumption failed with it. Fixed, and a genuine overdraw now says what it measured. The preview and the action now use one rule. A fully used lot read 'NaN%' instead of empty - 564 of 3,269 lots were in that state. A lot's material can be corrected from the vendor part it came from, and editing a vendor part's description now actually saves; every such edit made from the Catalog screen had been silently discarded. Locations: one location list instead of four inconsistent copies, you can add and correct locations yourself, and the cage shelf codes people have been typing into the notes field are now real locations you can filter and count by. Scheduling - the beginning of the end for Microsoft Project: a quote can now carry a real schedule built inside AOS, with tasks, dates, dependencies and hours, started from a template. When the quote is won that schedule BECOMES the project's schedule - not copied, not retyped, nothing lost. Templates now have published versions that never change underneath you: a schedule built from version 3 stays as built after somebody publishes version 5, and the project tells you it is on 3 with a plain list of what changed. Template steps can be edited at all now - previously you had to delete and re-add a step, which quietly broke every link pointing at it. The project timeline is editable: drag a phase to move it, drag an edge to change one date, and give a date to the rows that read 'not scheduled'. ARIA's real labour rates - every trade, every machine, and the fact that machines do not earn overtime - are recorded properly for the first time, with the dates each rate applied from. Fixes worth knowing: moving a bar on the timeline used to save twice, which also affected the Workforce Planner and the Department Hour Budgets editor; a milestone you created by hand could be deleted by a budget-window save, because AOS could not tell your milestones from the ones it generates; where two tasks depended on each other in a loop AOS reported that nothing downstream was affected - an all-clear that was not true - and could leave a schedule contradicting itself; and a schedule of several hundred tasks now opens about ten times faster because it only draws what is on screen. Quotes: the page is one column instead of two ragged ones, the top of a quote is a single card rather than three blocks repeating the same facts up to five times, and the calc sheet totals now sit under the document they were read from. Operations Intelligence: Projects is the first tab - it was shown as a sub-item of Quotes even though AOS already treated it as the page's home. Planner: manager controls that could silently vanish from a board you manage come back. This release also updates the database behind AOS, so please update as soon as you are prompted.
